sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:

practiceQuestions.q: In which year was the Congress-Khilafat Swaraj Party formed?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Swaraj Party was formed on January 1, 1923, following the Gaya session of the Congress in 1922. [Primary Reference: NCERT Themes in Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q: Who was the first President of the Swaraj Party?
practiceQuestions.sol: Chittaranjan Das (C.R. Das) was the President, and Motilal Nehru was the Secretary of the Swaraj Party. [Primary Reference: Spectrum Modern History]

practiceQuestions.q: Who served as the Secretary of the Swaraj Party at its inception?
practiceQuestions.sol: Motilal Nehru was the General Secretary of the Swaraj Party. [Primary Reference: NCERT Themes in Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q: The Swaraj Party was formed after the failure of which movement?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Swarajists wanted to enter the legislative councils after the withdrawal of the Non-Cooperation Movement following the Chauri Chaura incident. [Primary Reference: NCERT Themes in Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q: Which session of the Congress saw the split between 'Pro-changers' and 'No-changers'?
practiceQuestions.sol: The 1922 Gaya session, presided over by C.R. Das, witnessed the debate between those who wanted to enter councils and those who opposed it. [Primary Reference: Spectrum Modern History]

practiceQuestions.q: Who among the following was a 'No-changer'?
practiceQuestions.sol: Vallabhbhai Patel, Rajendra Prasad, and C. Rajagopalachari were prominent 'No-changers' who advocated for constructive work. [Primary Reference: NCERT Themes in Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the primary objective of the Swaraj Party?
opts: To boycott the British government completely
To enter legislative councils and obstruct government work
To support the British war effort
To establish a separate state for Muslims
practiceQuestions.sol: The Swarajists aimed to enter the councils to wreck the government from within by obstructing its policies. [Primary Reference: Spectrum Modern History]

practiceQuestions.q: Who became the first Indian to be elected as the President of the Central Legislative Assembly in 1925?
practiceQuestions.sol: Vithalbhai Patel, a prominent Swarajist, was elected President of the Central Legislative Assembly in 1925. [Primary Reference: NCERT Themes in Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q: The Swaraj Party was a faction within which larger organization?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Swaraj Party functioned as a group within the Indian National Congress. [Primary Reference: NCERT Themes in Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the 'constructive program' advocated by No-changers?
opts: Spinning Khadi and promoting Hindu-Muslim unity
practiceQuestions.sol: No-changers focused on constructive work like spinning, promoting Khadi, and social reform. [Primary Reference: NCERT Themes in Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q: Why did the Swarajists decide to enter the legislative councils?
opts: To cooperate with the British for reforms
To use the councils as a platform for political agitation
practiceQuestions.sol: They believed that if they could not end the councils, they would obstruct their working from within, exposing the hollowness of the 1919 Act. [Primary Reference: Spectrum Modern History]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the main point of contention between Pro-changers and No-changers?
opts: The role of the Khilafat movement
practiceQuestions.sol: The central debate was whether to boycott the councils (No-changers) or enter them (Pro-changers). [Primary Reference: NCERT Themes in Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q: How did the Swaraj Party's strategy change after the death of C.R. Das in 1925?
opts: They adopted a policy of responsive cooperation
They merged with the Muslim League
practiceQuestions.sol: After C.R. Das's death, the party faced internal divisions and adopted a policy of 'responsive cooperation' with the British. [Primary Reference: Spectrum Modern History]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the 'Responsive Cooperation' policy?
opts: Cooperating with the British only if they granted concessions
practiceQuestions.sol: Responsive cooperation meant cooperating with the government when it acted in the national interest and opposing it when it did not. [Primary Reference: Spectrum Modern History]

practiceQuestions.q: Why did the Swaraj Party eventually decline?
opts: Internal divisions and lack of a clear long-term goal
practiceQuestions.sol: The party suffered from internal rifts, the death of its leader C.R. Das, and the inability to maintain a consistent policy of obstruction. [Primary Reference: Spectrum Modern History]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the significance of the Swarajists' performance in the 1923 elections?
opts: They won a majority in the Central Legislative Assembly
They won a significant number of seats and paralyzed the government
practiceQuestions.sol: They won 42 out of 101 elected seats in the Central Legislative Assembly, which was a major success for a new party. [Primary Reference: NCERT Themes in Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q: How did the Swarajists view the 1919 Government of India Act?
opts: As a perfect framework for self-rule
As a sham that needed to be exposed
As a temporary measure to be accepted
As a document to be ignored
practiceQuestions.sol: They wanted to enter the councils to expose the 'sham' of the 1919 Act and show that it did not provide real power. [Primary Reference: Spectrum Modern History]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the 'Muddiman Committee' related to?
opts: Reviewing the working of the 1919 Act
practiceQuestions.sol: The Muddiman Committee was appointed to inquire into the working of the Dyarchy under the 1919 Act, which the Swarajists criticized. [Primary Reference: Spectrum Modern History]

practiceQuestions.q: Why did the Swarajists walk out of the legislatures in 1926?
opts: Because they were defeated in elections
Because the government refused to accept their demands for constitutional reform
Because they wanted to join the Civil Disobedience Movement
practiceQuestions.sol: In 1926, the Swarajists walked out of the legislatures as a protest against the government's refusal to concede to their demands for constitutional advancement. [Primary Reference: Spectrum Modern History]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the relationship between the Swaraj Party and the Khilafatists?
opts: They formed a coalition to challenge the British
The Khilafatists opposed the Swaraj Party
practiceQuestions.sol: The party was officially named the 'Congress-Khilafat Swaraj Party', reflecting the alliance between the Swarajists and the Khilafatists. [Primary Reference: NCERT Themes in Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Swaraj Party:
1. It was formed as a separate party outside the Congress.
2. It aimed to obstruct the working of the legislative councils.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Swaraj Party was formed as a group within the Congress, not as a separate party outside it. Statement 2 is correct. [Primary Reference: NCERT Themes in Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. C.R. Das was the President of the Swaraj Party.
2. Motilal Nehru was the Secretary of the Swaraj Party.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. C.R. Das was the President and Motilal Nehru was the Secretary. [Primary Reference: Spectrum Modern History]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the 'No-changers':
1. They advocated for the boycott of legislative councils.
2. They focused on constructive work like Khadi and spinning.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. No-changers followed the Gandhian path of constructive work and council boycott. [Primary Reference: NCERT Themes in Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Swaraj Party was formed after the Gaya session of the Congress.
2. The Gaya session was presided over by Motilal Nehru.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect because the Gaya session (1922) was presided over by C.R. Das. [Primary Reference: Spectrum Modern History]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Vithalbhai Patel was the first Indian to be elected as the President of the Central Legislative Assembly.
2. He was a member of the Swaraj Party.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Vithalbhai Patel was a prominent Swarajist leader. [Primary Reference: NCERT Themes in Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Swaraj Party advocated for 'Responsive Cooperation'.
2. This policy was adopted after the death of C.R. Das.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. The policy of responsive cooperation emerged as a response to internal rifts and the loss of leadership after 1925. [Primary Reference: Spectrum Modern History]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Swaraj Party was successful in completely wrecking the British administration.
2. The Swaraj Party failed to maintain unity among its members.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect as they could not completely wreck the administration. Statement 2 is correct as internal divisions led to their decline. [Primary Reference: Spectrum Modern History]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Swaraj Party was also known as the Congress-Khilafat Swaraj Party.
2. It was formed to continue the Non-Cooperation Movement.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect; it was formed after the withdrawal of the Non-Cooperation Movement to change the strategy, not to continue it in the same form. [Primary Reference: NCERT Themes in Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Swarajists were in favor of entering the legislative councils.
2. The No-changers were in favor of entering the legislative councils.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect as No-changers were against entering the councils. [Primary Reference: NCERT Themes in Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Swaraj Party was dissolved in 1935.
2. The Swaraj Party merged back into the Congress.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 2 is correct. The Swarajists eventually merged back into the Congress as the party lost its distinct identity and purpose. [Primary Reference: Spectrum Modern History]
